newsitem.title: CHINA: Two Mandarin hotel staff arrested in HK graft prob.
newsitem.headline: Two Mandarin hotel staff arrested in HK graft prob.

text.p: Hong Kong graft busters said on Thursday they had arrested two employees of the Mandarin hotel group and three contractors in a corruption probe.

A spokeswoman for the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) said the arrests were made in July in connection with corruption allegations, but she would reveal no further details at this stage because investigations were still under way.
"We did arrest five people in July. Two were from the works department of a hotel. Three were contractors," she said.

The two hotel employees, from Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group, the management company of the Singapore-listed Mandarin Oriental International Ltd (MOIL), were suspended after they were released on bail, a MOIL spokeswoman said.

MOIL, which operates 12 deluxe and first-class hotels mainly in the Asia-Pacific region, has two hotels in Hong Kong, The Excelsior and the flagship Mandarin Oriental, one of the world's most highly rated hotels.
The MOIL spokeswoman said the company viewed the investigation seriously.

"They (the two employees) have been suspended pending the outcome of investigations. We regard the matter very seriously as we do have a strict code of conduct here and we are working fully with the ICAC on the investigation," she said.

The Apple Daily newspaper, quoting unidentified sources, earlier reported that two hotel staff had taken HK$10 million ($1.29 million) in bribes related to renovation and maintenance contracts worth HK$100 million ($12.9 million).
